transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because something’s been going on at work for months. I’m a translator, and I keep seeing the same pattern in the project files. Certain subcontractors—and one colleague—make these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps, so it ends up looking like my quality control failed.

IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but I don’t believe that. The record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me.
Can you tell me more about why you believe your colleague and the subcontractors are trying to frame you?

Because it keeps showing up the same way. It’s not one big obvious change—it’s little things, like the translation memory being slightly altered or the timestamps lining up in a way that makes it look like I missed something in quality control.

And it’s the same people connected to those files: a few subcontractors and one colleague. When I question it, IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t convince me. The record can be made to look clean. I feel like it’s being arranged so that, if anyone checks later, it points back to me as the person who failed.
Have you had similar concerns or suspicions about others plotting against you or manipulating events in your life outside of work?

No, not really outside of work. It’s mainly this situation with the project files. For months I’ve been seeing the same pattern there—small changes in the translation memory, timestamps that line up in a way that makes it look like I missed quality control.

It’s tied to certain subcontractors and one colleague. That’s where I see it. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I don’t trust that, because the record can be arranged to look clean and still put the blame on me.
Have you ever seen, heard, or experienced things that others don’t seem to notice, like voices, visions, or other unusual sensations?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people don’t see. It’s more about the files and the records at work—what I’m noticing there.
Do you think these changes to the files are being made specifically to harm you or ruin your reputation at work?

Yes. I think that’s the point of it. It’s not just mistakes in the files. The way the translation memory and timestamps keep changing, it makes it look like I failed the quality control steps.

And it’s the same subcontractors and one colleague tied to it. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I don’t trust that. I think the record is being arranged so that if there’s a problem later, it points back to me and damages my reputation.
Do you think others at work believe the same way you do about these changes, or do you think you're the only one who sees this pattern?

I think I’m mostly the only one who’s really seeing the pattern. Other people may notice little issues, but they don’t seem to connect it the way I do.

To me it’s clear—the same subcontractors and one colleague, the small changes in the translation memory and the timestamps, and then it ends up looking like my quality control failed. Even if IT says the audit trail is clean, I don’t buy that completely. I think it’s been arranged so the blame lands on me.
Even though IT has told you the audit trail is clean, do you believe that no amount of evidence could prove to you that these changes aren't being made to frame you?

I wouldn’t say no amount of evidence, but… at this point, it would take a lot. IT saying the audit trail is clean doesn’t settle it for me.

I’ve been seeing the same pattern for months in the project files—the same subcontractors and one colleague, these tiny changes in the translation memory and timestamps, and then somehow it makes my quality control look like it failed. So when I’m told everything is clean, I still believe the record has been arranged so the blame lands on me.

Even though IT has told you the audit trail is clean and no one else seems to see the pattern you’re describing, do you feel certain that your interpretation is the only correct one, and that others are missing or ignoring the truth?

Yes, I do feel pretty certain. I know other people don’t seem to see it, or they accept what IT says, but that doesn’t change what I’ve been seeing for months.

It’s the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague making these small changes to the translation memory and timestamps, and then it ends up looking like my quality control failed. So when people say the audit trail is clean, I feel like they’re missing what’s really happening, or just choosing not to look closely enough. To me, the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.

Even though IT has told you the audit trail is clean and others don’t share your concern, do you believe that only you can see the truth and that no one else could possibly understand what’s really happening?

I don’t know if I’d say no one else could possibly understand. But yes, I do think I’m the one seeing it clearly.

I’ve been looking at these project files for months, and the same thing keeps happening—certain subcontractors and one colleague make these tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps, and then it looks like my quality control failed. So even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I still believe the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.

latest_inference.note: The patient's persistent, fixed belief that certain individuals are deliberately manipulating project files to frame them at work, despite reassurances from IT and lack of corroborating evidence, points toward a delusional disorder (F22.0). Schizophrenia (F20.0) is less likely due to absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms. Complex PTSD (F44.8) is also less likely as the focus is on a circumscribed delusional belief rather than trauma-related intrusions or hyperarousal. The belief remains unshakable despite contradictory evidence, making F22.0 the most accurate diagnosis at this point.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests concerns of persecution at work, possible delusional thinking, and possible impact on mood and functioning. Early candidates include delusional disorder, schizophrenia, major depressive disorder with severe features, dissociative disorders, and induced delusional disorder (folie à deux) as less likely differentials.
